newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Tuesday was quiet, with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
Bids were light at $62.00 to $63.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00, they said.
Last sales were at $64.00 late last week. Outlooks for this week's fed cattle trade were steady to $1.00 higher seen Wednesday or Thursday, market sources said.
"Right now the packer needs some cattle and would be willing to pay $64.00 to $65.00 to get it," said Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
Fed cattle prices were seen supported by firm beef prices and lighter finished cattle supplies, feedlot sources said.
Feedlot supplies this week were lighter compared with a week ago as reflected in estimated showlists, they said.

Showlists for the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area were pegged near 96,000 head, down about 1,500 from last week, the sources said. Showlists for Kansas were estimated near 86,500 head, down about 1,600.
The Nebraska showlist was estimated near 80,000, down 8,000, they said.
